answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Validating each node requires staking bonded deposits that scale superlinearly with cluster size: while a genuine pulse of single-agent activity remains cheap, registering an artificial swarm causes exponential capital exhaustion. Submitting proofs across dense layered shale consensus renders identity forging as fragile and unviable as shattered crystal under quadratic slashing.
